title: [4.9.3] podman ignores apparmor setting and lets host apparmor block in-container file access
body:
### Issue Description

I am currently stuck on Ubuntu 24 LTS and thus with podman 4.9.3. Please give a holler if this is fixed in a newer version, then I can go pester my admin to update me further "with due cause".

[Asked about it on Stack Exchange last week to no replies so far.](https://superuser.com/q/1939377/563952)

Trying to run a container with RHEL 9.5 and _no_ apparmor on my Ubuntu 24 LTS host with (as far as I know) vanilla apparmor settings, rsyslog inside the container fails, because all the custom file paths it has configured (e.g. `/etc/my/rsyslog.conf`, `/tmp/dev_log`, etc.) are being blocked by _the host system's_ apparmor.

In `sudo dmesg` I see that apparmor sees the files in question, as if they were part of the host filesystem - no wonder then, that it blocks them. E.g.
```
[71795.341479] audit: type=1400 audit(1786094015.729:247): apparmor="DENIED" operation="open" class="file" profile="rsyslogd" name="/etc/my/rsyslog.conf" pid=51335 comm="rsyslogd" requested_mask="r" denied_mask="r" fsuid=10999 ouid=447900762
[71795.342660] audit: type=1400 audit(1786094015.731:248): apparmor="DENIED" operation="mknod" class="file" profile="rsyslogd" name="/tmp/dev_log" pid=51335 comm="rsyslogd" requested_mask="c" denied_mask="c" fsuid=10999 ouid=10999
```

How do I get podman to isolate the container as the black box it is supposed to be? Why would host apparmor even see these files or their using process and _why would it see the in-container path!?!?_

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. start a container without apparmor  
=> rsyslog inside the container crashes with 'permission denied' errors
2. `sudo dmesg`  
=> apparmor _on the host_ has blocked access to a file with the same path, which does not exist on the host and is not accessed on the host
3. add file path inside the container to apparmor profile _outside the container_ and repeat step 1  
=> error disappears for this file, new error appears for the next file
4. `podman run --security-opt apparmor=unconfined [etc.]` and repeat step 1  
=> no change


### Describe the results you received

Container does not work on Ubuntu 24 LTS host. Container works fine on RHEL 9.5 host (which has no apparmor).
`--security-opt apparmor=unconfined` has no effect **and does not produce any error**!!!

### Describe the results you expected

- NEVER FAIL SILENTLY, please. Produce an error I can report (or ideally an actionable error message I can resolve myself, but admittedly that is often hard and not always viable at all).
- Container should be a blackbox, outside of podman neither the in-container rsyslog nor the in-container file nor any in-container path should be visible to apparmor _or any other program_, unless explicitly forwarded.
- Container that works on one host should work on all hosts - that's what containers are for.

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

No

### Additional environment details

- As far as I know, my apparmor and podman settings are all fully vanilla _for Ubuntu 24 LTS_.   Which is to say: They are probably wrong, Ubuntu is known to do that in its packages, but I have no idea what to look for. Also, I have an administrator. Who knows what they change or -d.
- I see the warnings mentioned in #23808 but presumably they are not related, or more people would report this problem (I hope).
  - But some do. [[1](https://github.com/ansible/awx/issues/14259#issuecomment-1773581125)][[2](https://github.com/ansible/awx/pull/15717#issuecomment-2552681004)]

### Additional information

This was not an issue on Ubuntu 22 LTS with podman 3.4.4. But due to the large gap between 22 and 24, I have no idea whether the podman version is to blame for it, or something else.

All I can say is that the OS update introduced the problem for me.

comments.body:
You need to report this against ubuntu not upstream. First, we only support the latest version but also we have no apparmor expert on our team which could even help you debug.

Rootless podman atm does not apply a custom profile to the container process so this is all just standard distro profiles at play here. We do not ship any apparmor profile for podman itself so this is all up to the distribution package to ensure things work.

I mean, okay, but how does apparmour _outside_ even see that something in the container called 'rsyslog' is trying to access pathes, that do not even exist outside?

_There is no path_ /etc/my/rsyslog.conf on my host machine, there is none! - If not from podman, how could apparmor possibly be informed about it? And if _by_ podman, using a non-existing path is just straight-up malicious.

Surely that it is apparmor is purely incidental? And that podman silently ignores the `--security-opt apparmor=unconfined` _without any error message_ is surely not apparmour's fault either?

... Ah well, I will try my luck at the distribution level, thank you for your time.

> And that podman silently ignores the --security-opt apparmor=unconfined without any error message is surely not apparmour's fault either?

It is not ignored at all, that is how it is already running when running at rootless. The system policy still applies as we cannot just bypass that obviously.

Apparmor liekly resoles the in container paths against the system policies on your system.
I guess that based on https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28578

long term I guess someone would need to fix https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/15874 to actually be able to load custom profile for the rootless container.

But as I said we have no apparmor expertise on our team so this needs to be driven by other people.

That background information helps a lot and I do not think I could have found it on my own.

Thank you.
